-- 103_source_scans_and_ledger.sql
-- SCHEMA migration — a record of each READING of a source, and the source-by-parameter
-- ledger derived from it. Tooling T1 (owner approval D8, 2026-10-09);
-- catalogue-plan-v2 section 3.8, critique finding F13.
--
-- THE GAP. Nothing recorded which source had been read for which parameter. A parameter
-- promoted in month three was never looked for in month one's sources, and the catalogue
-- could imply "no code sets a requirement" where nobody had read the code for that
-- quantity -- while every gate read green. That is how GAP-061's lost figures happened.
-- The owner's requirement it answers, 2026-10-09: "Ensure that we can add and expand
-- parameter catalogue as required based on new information we come across."
--
-- ONE ROW PER READING, NOT ONE ROW PER (SOURCE, PARAMETER). Parameter numbers are never
-- reused (base_parameters is AUTOINCREMENT, migration 076), so a reading that stores the
-- highest parameter_id existing when it was made says exactly which parameters it could
-- have covered: "catalogue version N" means "parameters 1..N, those active at the time".
-- Silence is then DERIVED by the view below; nobody writes an `absent` extraction for
-- every pair, and explicit `absent` rows stay for positive statements of absence.
--
-- `catalogue_version` IS COMPUTED BY THE WRITER, NEVER TYPED (CLAUDE.md rule 8):
-- `db.py record-scan` reads MAX(parameter_id) at call time and refuses a typed value.
-- `pages_read`/`pages_total` are computed the same way, from the page markers of the
-- file read (retrieval_log.page_coverage), and `file_sha256` must name a file the
-- retrieval-log manifests hold for this source. The CHECKs below hold the invariants for
-- every writer, including a data migration that does not go through db.py.
--
-- STAGE: evidence (governance/stage-map.yaml) -- what was read of an admitted source,
-- beside its extraction rows.
--
-- WHAT READS IT (CLAUDE.md section 8): `v_scan_ledger` below; the batch rule R16-scan in
-- scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py (every admission has a catalogue-mode reading);
-- scripts/audit/scan_debt.py through the view. Not built and not read here: a reading
-- does not prove the reader saw everything -- adversarial standing subject 4 samples
-- each source for figures no row carries.

CREATE TABLE source_scans (
    -- AUTOINCREMENT, as 076 did for the other ids a record names: a scan_id is cited by
    -- session records and must never come to mean a different reading.
    scan_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    ref_id              TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
    -- catalogue: every active parameter up to catalogue_version.
    -- targeted:  one parameter, target_parameter_id (a back-fill reading).
    mode                TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (mode IN ('catalogue', 'targeted')),
    catalogue_version   INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (catalogue_version >= 1),
    target_parameter_id INTEGER REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),
    -- full: the whole document. partial: some pages of it. fragment: one page or clause
    -- of a larger instrument. abstract: an abstract or metadata record only.
    text_scope          TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (text_scope IN
                                ('full', 'partial', 'fragment', 'abstract')),
    pages_read          INTEGER CHECK (pages_read IS NULL OR pages_read >= 0),
    pages_total         INTEGER CHECK (pages_total IS NULL OR pages_total >= 1),
    -- Which saved file was read, by checksum: the manifest's own sha256 of the bytes.
    file_sha256         TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (length(file_sha256) = 64),
    -- Whether the open pass (quantities the catalogue lacks, plan section 3.4) was done
    -- in this reading.
    open_pass_done      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (open_pass_done IN (0, 1)),
    -- full-read: the text was read against the list. pre-screen: only a script listed
    -- where catalogue terms occur -- weaker, and v_scan_ledger says which it was.
    method              TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('full-read', 'pre-screen')),
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT    NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT,
    CHECK ((mode = 'targeted' AND target_parameter_id IS NOT NULL)
        OR (mode = 'catalogue' AND target_parameter_id IS NULL)),
    CHECK (pages_read IS NULL OR pages_total IS NULL OR pages_read <= pages_total),
    -- "full" over a paged text means every page; a reading of fewer pages is partial.
    CHECK (text_scope <> 'full' OR pages_read IS NULL OR pages_read = pages_total)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_source_scans_ref ON source_scans(ref_id);

CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
--
--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
--                     never read again; its replacement is.
--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).

plan ("any `stated` cell whose governing set includes a source with no extraction
    for that parameter -- do not merge the migration"): after this change that cell is
    not merely forbidden, it is unconstructible. Every ref_id in the governing set
    came out of this query, and this query returns only sources that hold an
    extraction for the parameter being determined.

    ONLY VALUE-SUPPLYING ROWS GOVERN (added 2026-09-13, migration 075's whole point).
    Holding an extraction for the parameter was never enough. Measured on the live
    corpus the day the grading landed: specification 1 was `stated` at T1 -- the
    strongest claim this project makes -- on four rows of which TWO WERE CONDITIONS
    (the slopes a treadmill was set to; the ADA range a study tested) and two were
    findings, one of them `claim_type='absent'`, asserting nothing whatever. Not one
    governing row was a claim. Specification 2 was the same shape.

    So the predicate is `figure_role IN ('claim','derived')`:

      claim     -- the row states a value for the parameter. Governs.
      derived   -- the row's value was computed from other rows. Governs; its band
                   is the floored mean of its inputs' (owner ruling 2026-09-13).
      finding   -- the row reports something ABOUT the parameter without asserting a
                   value: "code-compliant width fails 10-100% of users". Supplies
                   DIRECTION, never value (owner ruling 2026-09-13). Not gathered here.
      condition -- a rig setting or a limit the value is conditioned by. Never anchors.
      NULL      -- ungraded. Not a value-supplier: a row nobody has stated the kind of
                   cannot be read as a claim, which is exactly how a tested slope came
                   to govern a `stated` cell.

    A cell whose value-supplying set is empty now comes out `pending`, which for both
    live cells is the truth -- not one retrieved source states a corridor width or a
    ramp gradient value. Gathering `finding` rows for direction, and the `confirms`
    edge that upgrades a code value, build ON this predicate and are not required by
    it.
    """
    # NOT-PUBLISHABLE METHODS ARE NOT GATHERED (owner 2026-10-09: "skimmed values are not
    # publishable"). A source whose only value-supplying rows were skimmed does not enter
    # the governing set; gather_extraction_links records each skimmed row as excluded with
    # the reason. Fixture tolerance as above: a synthetic table without the column has no
    # skimmed rows to leave out.
    skim, skim_params = _publishable_clause(conn, "x")
    return _gather(conn, "", f"x.figure_role IN ('claim', 'derived') {skim}",
                   (parameter_id, *skim_params))


def _has_column(conn, table, column):
    """Fixture tolerance: does this database's `table` carry `column`?"""
    return any(r[1] == column for r in conn.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{table}")'))

# --- R16-scan: every admission is READ against the whole catalogue ----------------
    # Added 2026-10-09, tooling T1 (owner approval D8 of catalogue-plan-v2 section 4.2),
    # for the owner's requirement of the same day: "Slugs guide our searches, but they do
    # not guide what we derive and mine from sources!" R11-harvest and R16 read rows that
    # exist; neither can tell a source read against every parameter from one read for the
    # one parameter its slug was about, which is how GAP-061's figures were lost. The
    # reading record (source_scans, migration 103) makes the difference a row: each
    # admission owes at least one CATALOGUE-mode reading (any text scope -- an abstract is
    # read at abstract scope, and v_scan_ledger shows the difference). A targeted reading
    # covers one parameter and does not discharge it. A tombstone is never read again
    # (record-scan refuses one), so a superseded admission is out of the subject.
    #
    # GRANDFATHERED BY DATE IN A BATCH RUN, COUNTED IN --all. No reading could be recorded
    # before source_scans existed, so a batch admitted earlier would fail a rule it could
    # not have met -- and research_dod_session is BLOCKING on LATEST-RESEARCH (the batch it
    # names). Admissions created before R16_SCAN_FROM are therefore REPORTED in a
    # batch run, not failed; --all counts them all against the baseline, which ratchets
    # down as the re-reading phase (plan section 7, P3) records their readings. The same
    # forward-commitment shape as alias_provenance_audit's CUTOFF_SESSION_DATE. A row with
    # no created_at is treated as owed (stricter, not looser).
    grandfathered = []
    if _rows(cx, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='source_scans'")[0][0]:
        cat_read = ("EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_scans s WHERE s.ref_id = e.ref_id "
                    "AND s.mode = 'catalogue')")
        live_adm = " AND e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL"
        if allmode:
            owed_rows = _rows(cx, "SELECT e.ref_id, " + cat_read + " FROM evidence_sources e "
                              "WHERE 1=1" + live_adm + escope + " ORDER BY e.ref_id", sargs)
        else:
            owed_rows = _rows(cx, "SELECT e.ref_id, " + cat_read + " FROM evidence_sources e "
                              "WHERE COALESCE(e.created_at, '9999') >= ?" + live_adm + escope
                              + " ORDER BY e.ref_id", (R16_SCAN_FROM,) + sargs)
            grandfathered = [r[0] for r in _rows(
                cx, "SELECT e.ref_id FROM evidence_sources e WHERE e.created_at < ? "
                    "AND NOT " + cat_read + live_adm + escope + " ORDER BY e.ref_id",
                (R16_SCAN_FROM,) + sargs)]
        scan_owed = len(owed_rows)
        missing_reads = [r[0] for r in owed_rows if not r[1]]
        gf_txt = ("; REPORTED, not asserted: %d admission(s) predate the reading record "
                  "(created before %s) and carry no catalogue reading: %s -- the re-reading "
                  "phase owes them" % (len(grandfathered), R16_SCAN_FROM,
                                       ", ".join(grandfathered[:8]))

                 "source against the WHOLE parameter list, whatever slug it came in under, "
                 "and record it: python3 scripts/research/full_text.py --ref-id R --session "
                 "S (when a PDF or web page is held), then db.py record-scan --ref-id R "
                 "--mode catalogue --file-sha256 <sha> --text-scope ... --method full-read%s"

        else:

CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
--
--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
--                     never read again; its replacement is.
--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).
--
-- STATUS PRECEDENCE, first match wins:
--   1 EXTRACTED          a non-absent extraction exists for the pair (any figure_role).
--   2 STATED-ABSENT      only claim_type 'absent' extractions exist: the source addresses
--                        the quantity and sets nothing -- a positive statement.
--   3 READ-NOTHING-FOUND a FULL-scope reading covers the pair and found no row.
--   4 READ-PARTIAL       only partial / fragment / abstract readings cover it.
--   5 NOT-READ           no reading covers it.
-- A reading COVERS a pair when it is catalogue-mode with catalogue_version >=
-- parameter_id (the parameter existed when the reading was made), or targeted at that
-- parameter. Rows 1 and 2 win over readings because a row written is stronger evidence
-- than a reading recorded; 3 wins over 4 because a full reading supersedes a partial
-- one of the same source.
--
-- scan_id / text_scope / method name the STRONGEST covering reading (full scope first,
-- then full-read before pre-screen, then the latest), so a READ-NOTHING-FOUND resting on
-- a pre-screen only is visible as such. NULL when no reading covers the pair.
WITH pairs AS (
    SELECT e.ref_id, p.parameter_id
      FROM evidence_sources e
     CROSS JOIN base_parameters p
     WHERE e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
       AND p.status = 'active'
),
best AS (
    SELECT pr.ref_id, pr.parameter_id,
           (SELECT s.scan_id FROM source_scans s
             WHERE s.ref_id = pr.ref_id
               AND ((s.mode = 'catalogue' AND s.catalogue_version >= pr.parameter_id)
                 OR (s.mode = 'targeted' AND s.target_parameter_id = pr.parameter_id))
             ORDER BY (s.text_scope = 'full') DESC, (s.method = 'full-read') DESC,
                      s.scan_id DESC
             LIMIT 1) AS scan_id
      FROM pairs pr
)
SELECT b.ref_id,
       b.parameter_id,
       CASE
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type <> 'absent') THEN 'EXTRACTED'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type = 'absent') THEN 'STATED-ABSENT'
         WHEN s.text_scope = 'full' THEN 'READ-NOTHING-FOUND'
         WHEN s.scan_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'READ-PARTIAL'
         ELSE 'NOT-READ'
       END AS status,
       b.scan_id,
       s.text_scope,
       s.method
  FROM best b
  LEFT JOIN source_scans s ON s.sc

return out


#: NOTATIONS OF ONE QUANTITY, and the arithmetic that relates them. Owner ruling
#: 2026-09-17: "Present both -- don't choose between ratio or percentage."
#:
#: THIS IS A DEFINITION, NOT A CURATED FACT, which is why it is a literal here and
#: not derived from the corpus (CLAUDE.md rule 8 asks for derivation of facts the
#: machine can compute; the relation between `1:20` and `5 %` is mathematics and
#: there is nothing in the database to read it off).
#:
#: A FAMILY IS NOT A UNIT. Members are two ways of WRITING one dimensionless
#: quantity. Millimetres and degrees are different units, and the ruling says so in
#: its own ACTION (4): composing across THEM stays refused. Adding a member here is
#: a claim that two notations denote the same quantity exactly, which is a
#: mathematical claim and should be made deliberately.
NOTATION_FAMILIES = {
    "gradient": ("%", "rise:run ratio"),
}
#: Every family member MUST appear here, and the guard below refuses one that does
#: not. Without it, adding a notation to the tuple above and forgetting the
#: arithmetic makes `to_canonical` fall through to `Fraction(text)` and read the
#: number AS IF it were already canonical -- `5` degrees silently becoming `5 %`.
#: That is the shape a reviewer of the 2026-09-17 ruling flagged: `degrees` is the
#: ARCTANGENT of the ratio, not a rescaling of it, so it is not a notation of this
#: quantity at all and belongs to a family of its own or to none. Membership is a
#: mathematical claim; this makes forgetting to back it up an error rather than a
#: wrong answer.
_CONVERTIBLE = {"%", "rise:run ratio"}
_RATIO_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*:\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*$")


def notation_family(unit):
    """Which family a stated unit belongs to, or None if it stands alone."""
    for fam, members in NOTATION_FAMILIES.items():
        if (unit or "").strip() in members:
            return fam
    return None


def to_canonical(raw, unit):
    """One stated value -> an exact Fraction on its family's canonical scale.

    The canonical scale is the family's FIRST member -- percent for gradient -- and
    the conversion is exact because it is done in Fraction, never float: `1:12` is
    100/12, which is 8.333... and is never rounded here. Rounding happens once, at
    render, and is marked inexact when it happens.
    """
    txt = (raw or "").strip()
    if not txt:
        return None
    fam = notation_family(unit)
    if fam and (unit or "").strip() not in _CONVERTIBLE:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "%r is listed in NOTATION_FAMILIES[%r] but no conversion is defined for "
            "it. A family member is a claim that two notations denote ONE quantity "
            "exactly; back it with arithmetic in to_canonical/from_canonical, or "
            "remove it. Falling through here would read the number as if it were "
            "already canonical." % (unit, fam))
    m = _RATIO_RE.match(txt)
    if m and fam:
        rise, run = Fraction(m.group(1)), Fraction(m.group(2))
        if run == 0:
            return None
        return rise / run * 100                      # rise:run -> percent, exactly
    try:
        return (None, v)
    return (v, v)


def parse_bound(claimed_value, comparator, claim_type):
    """One governing claim -> (lo, hi) in its own unit, or None if it states no number.

    The comparator IS the bound, which is why migration 075 added it: "more than thirty
    centimetres" stored as a bare 30 turns a floor into a point, and a determination built
    from points is a determination that has quietly dropped every inequality its sources
    stated.

      =, approx, or no comparator on a numerical claim -> a point:   (v, v)
      >=, >                                            -> a floor:   (v, None)
      <=, <                                            -> a ceiling: (None, v)
      between, or a range claim written "a to b"       -> (a, b)

    STRICTNESS IS NOT MODELLED, deliberately. `>` and `>=` both land as (v, None): the
    columns are REAL and carry no open/closed flag, and inventing one here would put a
    distinction in the determination that no render surface can show and no source states
    precisely enough to defend. The comparator stays on the extraction, which is where a
    reader can see it.

    Returns None for anything that is not a number -- a qualitative claim, a ratio like
    '1:12', a value with words in it. Those govern the STATE of a cell (they are still
    `figure_role='claim'`) without contributing a numeric bound, and the caller says so
    rather than silently treating them as zero.
    """
    raw = (claimed_value or "").strip()
    if not raw:
        return None
    cmp_ = (comparator or "").strip()

    def num(tok):
        try:
            return float(tok)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return None

    if cmp_ == "between" or claim_type == "range":
        parts = re.split(r"\s+to\s+|\s*-\s*|\s*–\s*", raw)
        if len(parts) == 2:
            lo, hi = num(parts[0]), num(parts[1])
            if lo is not None and hi is not None:
                return (min(lo, hi), max(lo, hi))
        return None
    v = num(raw)
    if v is None:
        return None
    if cmp_ in (">=", ">"):
        return (v, None)
    if cmp_ in ("<=", "<"):
        return (None, v)
    return (v, v)
